meta: Fachang Muqi's Willow and Magpie of the mid-1200s, done in ink to suggest the bird, the willow, rain and mist.
about: The museum says Willow and Magpie comes from close knowledge of birds in general and magpies in particular, joined to a sophisticated ink technique that suggests the nature of the bird, the character of willow, and the look of rain and mist. It sets these skills beside Southern Song achievements in lyric poetry and canal building. Fachang Muqi made the hanging scroll in the mid-1200s.

meta: Saint John embraces the Christ child beside two pomegranates in Francesco Torbido's Holy Family with Saint Catherine, about 1525.
about: The Holy Family with Saint Catherine sit in a landscape. The child Saint John the Baptist embraces the Christ child, and two pomegranates lie at his feet. An angel with a lily branch stands between Joseph and Mary. Francesco Torbido painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1525.

meta: Kannon looks at the moon in the water, holding a willow branch and vase, in a painting attributed to the Zen monk Gakuō Zōkyū, about 1500.
about: This painting of Kannon, the Buddhist deity of mercy and compassion, is attributed to Gakuō Zōkyū, a well-known Zen monk who specialized in ink painting. Kannon looks at the moon reflected in water, a symbol of impermanence. The willow branch and water vase in her hands stand for healing and purification.

meta: Johann Wilhelm Kaiser, graphic artist and director of the Rijksmuseum, in a bust portrait by Pantaleon Szyndler, 1875.
about: Johann Wilhelm Kaiser, who lived from 1813 to 1900, was a graphic artist and director of the Engraving School and of the Rijksmuseum. He is shown in a bust portrait turned to the right. Pantaleon Szyndler painted it in 1875.

meta: Maharaja Pratap Singh of Jaipur, patron of the Palace of the Winds, in a colored ink portrait by Sahib Ram of about 1793.
about: Pratap Singh took the throne of the princely state of Jaipur in 1778 at 14, about 15 years before this portrait. A poet and patron of the arts, he was known for commissioning the Palace of the Winds, and he kept a studio of about 50 painters, among them the Muslim master Sahib Ram, to whom this portrait is attributed. He was a devotee of the god Krishna, and the mark on his forehead shows it.

meta: Xiao Yi gets the Lanting Manuscript by trickery, a painting traditionally given to Qian Xuan about Wang Xizhi's famous Preface.
about: This painting concerns the Preface of the Lanting Gathering, written by the calligrapher Wang Xizhi, who lived around 303 to 361, while he was with eminent scholars and poets who drank wine as they worked beside a winding brook among bamboo groves and mountains. The museum introduces it through Wen Zhengming, a Ming painter, calligrapher and scholar who excelled in all the major scripts and most often wrote semicursive script in Wang's style. The painting is traditionally attributed to Qian Xuan.

meta: William Howard Taft, twenty-seventh president, painted by William Valentine Schevill around 1910.
about: Days after William Howard Taft was elected president, Theodore Roosevelt told a colleague that Taft's policies, principles, purposes and ideals were the same as his own. Taft kept regulating big business and brought ninety-nine antitrust cases, but Roosevelt grew disappointed in his handpicked heir. Part of his frustration came from the Tariff Act of 1909, which raised some tariffs and only slightly lowered others. William Valentine Schevill painted this portrait of the 27th president, who served from 1909 to 1913.

meta: Workers on their lunch break around a horse-drawn bakery wagon under big factories in Carl Gaertner's The Pie Wagon, about 1926.
about: Carl Gaertner was one of the most widely exhibited artists working in Cleveland, and he specialized in painting the city and its surroundings. His favorite subjects included scenes of Cleveland's industrial heyday, such as this one. He focuses on laborers who spend their lunch break milling around a horse-drawn bakery wagon in the shadows of looming factories. The logo on the wagon marks it as the Star Bakery, a flourishing Cleveland business then.

meta: A festoon of grapes, apricots, oranges and peaches with a butterfly and a wasp, painted by Johannes Borman in 1653.
about: A festoon of different fruits, among them grapes, apricots, oranges and peaches, hangs in this picture, and a butterfly and a wasp fly around it. Johannes Borman painted it in 1653, and the Rijksmuseum holds it.

meta: A page from a Persian Five Treasures of Jami owned by the Mughal vizier Abd al-Rahim, with borders he commissioned.
about: This page comes from a prized manuscript owned by Abd al-Rahim, one of the most respected statesmen of the Mughal court and vizier under Akbar and Jahangir. He loved books and the arts. He bought this copy of Jami's five long narrative poems, which include the rhymed romance of Joseph and the Egyptian lady Zulaykha, about 80 years after it was finished. Its illumination was unfinished, so he had the lively decoration of the borders added. The painter is given as Mushfiq.
credit_line: Gift in honor of Madeline Neves Clapp; Gift of Mrs. Henry White Cannon by exchange; Bequest of Louise T. Cooper; Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund; From the Catherine and Ralph Benkaim Collection

meta: Waves crash on rocks at night with a lighthouse light in the distance in Robert C. Minor's Great Silas at Night, 1890.
about: Robert Minor made a small but dramatic nighttime picture of waves crashing against rocks. He was living in Greenwich Village in 1890, and the view may be of the New York or Connecticut coast. A pinpoint of light from a lighthouse is just visible in the distance, which makes the waves look bigger and shows the danger for ships off the coast.

meta: Maharaja Anup Singh of Bikaner receives a courtier in an informal study by Ruknuddin, about 1690.
about: This informal study shows Maharaja Anup Singh of Bikaner, who reigned from 1669 to 1698, receiving a courtier. Ruknuddin was one of the most celebrated artists of the Bikaner painting studio, and the museum says even a spontaneous sketch shows his mastery of brushwork and portraiture. He was a second cousin of Nur Muhammad, who made the portrait drawing of Maharaja Rai Singh of Bikaner. White areas mark places where Ruknuddin made corrections, such as the king's right foot.
credit_line: Purchase and partial gift from the Catherine and Ralph Benkaim Collection; Severance and Greta Millikin Purchase Fund

meta: A solitary crane stands in a bamboo grove in Tao Hong's album leaf of the early 1600s, the poetic half of a pair.
about: Tao Hong was a versatile artist, little known today. The first leaf of this pair shows farmers returning home after a day in the fields, and this one is more poetic: a lone crane stands in a bamboo grove. The museum says Tao Hong uses light colors and nuanced brushwork to get an effect of natural light and luminosity. He made the leaf in the early 1600s.
credit_line: Gift of Dr. and Mrs. Sherman E. Lee

meta: Scholars say goodbye at a riverbank while servants pack up the farewell party in Yao Shou's handscroll, Parting at the Gate of the Capital.
about: This handscroll captures a goodbye. A boatman stands tall on the riverbank with his paddle ready to launch, and scholars in black hats linger over their parting nearby. In a thatched pavilion two servants pack up what is left of a farewell party. In ancient China a handscroll was viewed by unrolling it one arm's length at a time from right to left, so the travelers and the distant landscape came into view gradually. Yao Shou made it in the 15th century.

meta: Maids struggle to detain travelers at twilight in Hiroshige's Goyu, from The Fifty-Three Stations of the Tokaido Road.
about: This village street at twilight is the scene of Goyu. In the center maidservants struggle to get hold of travelers, and at the right a traveler in an open teahouse gets ready to wash his feet. The names of the engraver, printer, designer and publisher are written on its walls. It is from Hiroshige's series The Fifty-Three Stations of the Tokaido Road.
